title: A fantasy skirmish board game based on Christian Mythology - Deliverance Review
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=FfCJfpHXt8c

Daniel (@dungeondive) frames Deliverance, a tactical skirmish game from Lowen Games in which angels fight demons over the town of Fallbrook, with a reading list of religion-rooted genre fiction: Edward M. Erdelac's Merkabah Rider, Philip K. Dick's VALIS trilogy, A Canticle for Leibowitz, Journey to the West, William Peter Blatty, and the inevitable This Present Darkness. The review runs in two parts. First, the game, which he rates a genuinely excellent skirmish design in the Final Fantasy Tactics mould. Nine angels each carry 15 unique talents across three tiers, heavenly treasure to equip, courage as a currency and a prayer deck of spells; Sardius moves one square but drags three targets across the board, while another angel lays healing light tiles. Demons act in groups off d6 tables, bosses bring their own decks, and minor and major talents scale difficulty. Saints are contested terrain that flip between oppressed and protected. Second, the preachiness question raised on the channel's Facebook group. Raised by two liberal ministers and a Christian for 25 years, Daniel finds the Bible verses easy to read as mythology and the game no cheap cash-in. His one real objection is the Darkness deck, where cards named Sexual Immorality, Manic Depression and Suicidal Thoughts cast real illnesses and consenting adults as demonic affliction. He would have preferred creepy art and a game effect, no labels.

----

Daniel separates a well-made game from the values printed on one of its decks. Where do you draw that line when a game's theme sits uneasily with you?
